propositions: Nested pytest child launched without --basetemp joins user-global numbered temp root, causing session-finish cleanup to scan and recursively delete unrelated stale entries that can consume the 90-second timeout after test execution completes.

With 400,000+ stale entries in shared numbered root, child cleanup takes 10.8s vs 0.882s with private basetemp, proving cleanup cost scales with retained entries and violates the helper's isolation invariant.
Nested pytest child must receive a caller-owned tmp_path/nested-pytest via --basetemp to isolate session-finish cleanup while preserving ambient tracker HEAD/directories and test selection.
Omitting --basetemp allows nested pytest to delete another run's sentinel files and temp trees, violating the contract that ambient state remains unchanged.
